title: Cello
summary: Cello notes played through a computed cello body. Limits first: A3 and the low notes are too dark, several notes are too clean, and the stopped notes sit off pitch. Every note drives a computed spruce and maple shell body with an air cavity, a finite-width hair bow, the measured rosin friction law of Woodhouse and Galluzzo (2025, eq. 13) and the printed 116 mm after-length. E2 sits 5.8 c flat of equal temperament and E3 6.7 c flat between its dips (the median in 0.1 s windows over 0.6-1.95 s; the grader's pitch reads it 8.1 c flat), each after one finger move and one residual-flexibility row and with its bow moved to 1/11 of its sounding length; F5's bow is at 1/11 too, which removes its line at a third of its pitch but leaves it 7 dB too clean. Eb4 is rendered at 47944 Hz to remove time-step lines, plays with the body's wood loss raised 3.25 times, near the printed damping, and has its bow at 1/11 of its sounding length too; with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs it scores 9 of 14 where it scored 11 with 6-layer ribs: its harmonics and short-time spectrum cross their rulers outward, its fifth and sixth harmonics rise 8.5 and 5.9 dB to sit 2.3 and 4.2 dB over the recording's (re the first, 0.5-1.6 s), its eighth falls 15.7 dB to 33.0 dB under it, and above 5 kHz it reads -61.5 dB re total against -32.1 dB in the recording; its line at 301 Hz falls 7 dB, to 46 dB under its first harmonic, its note is 1.3 dB too clean where it was 3.8, and its attack reads 437 ms against 411. D3 carries its string's measured torsion (758 Hz, 1.8 kg/s, Q 34), which moves it 1.0 c flat and off the render clock; on the body with the endpin and the printed bar its attack reads 387 ms against 381, from a shelf 3 to 6 dB under the held level to 0.35 s rather than the recording's slow rise, and its first two harmonics stay swapped; with the cello's other three strings (C2, G2, A3) unbowed on its bridge it scores 14 of 14 as before, its second harmonic goes from 4.6 dB over the first to 10.3 dB under it (the recording's is 7.5 dB under) and its centroid from 358 to 311 Hz (the recording's is 215), but the shelf is gone and its attack reads 91 ms, its note reads 11.6 dB too dirty where it was 4.1, and a line at 198.3 Hz rings at -33 dB re its first harmonic, 11 dB over the recording's strongest low line. C2 now plays the s8 shell the other pages play, with the endpin, the printed bar and its ribs meshed in 24 layers: it scores 7 of 14 (8 on its old shell, 6 on the s8 shell with 6-layer ribs), and its 11th and 12th harmonics sit 32 and 34 dB under the recording's, re its third. G2 carries the endpin and the printed bar too and, with the cello's other three strings (D3, C2, A3) unbowed on its bridge, scores 13 of 14 where it scored 11: its first harmonics come down toward the recording's (the second from 13.2 dB over the first to 2.5 dB over it; the recording's is 5.2 dB under) and its top band comes up 8 dB, but a D3 string rings at 146 Hz at -31 dB, its note reads 5.3 dB too dirty where it was 2.3 dB too clean, and its eighth harmonic opens a hole 23 dB under the recording's. E2 carries the endpin and the printed bar too, and with its ribs meshed in 24 layers it scores 5 of 14 where it scored 8 with 6-layer ribs: its level still holds and its second harmonic still leads its first, but it reads 13 dB too clean (harmonics-to-noise 43.2 dB against 30.1), and its spectral distance and band envelope cross their rulers outward. E3 now carries the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs as well and scores 5 of 14 where it scored 6: its odd/even balance crosses its ruler outward, its start is fast (-3 dB re the held level at 0.1 s, against 0.375 s in the recording), and three times in the clip its pitch drops for 0.1 to 0.25 s, to as much as 23.5 c flat of equal temperament, where it otherwise holds 4.6 to 7.8 c flat; with the endpin and the bar on 6-layer ribs (a render not posted) it did neither, and why the rib does this is not known. D3 and A3 keep 512 body modes, the others 256.
physics_present: a computed cello shell body from published plate geometry and wood data: spruce top, maple back and ribs, a 12.5 mm-class table, a 19 g bridge and 256 computed modes (D3 and A3 keep 512; D3's last mode is about 4.3 kHz); on C2, E2, E3 and Eb4 the ribs are meshed in 24 layers (5.1 mm), the most the shell's per-component cap admits, because 12 layers were not converged (from 12 to 24 layers the first 100 coupled modes moved a median 0.60 % and modes 101 to 257 1.61 %, against limits of 0.3 and 1 % registered before the runs); whether 24 layers is converged is not measured, and the other pages keep 6 layers (20.3 mm)
an enclosed air cavity through a physical neck, and f-holes placed from printed caliper measurements of the Castelbarco Stradivari (Library of Congress)
the measured Kaplan string rows (Mansour 2016): tension, mass, bending stiffness and loss factors for the string played, with the bridge and bow flexibility

the exact static residual flexibility of each string's omitted bending modes (`residual-flexibility exact-static-green`): the row adds the string's omitted modes as one static compliance at the bridge and at a finger, with no fitted number; A3, C2, D3 and G2 carry it with its bow counterpart, E2 and E3 carry the support row alone (it takes the E3 note 4.5 c flat and its 180 Hz line down 11.6 dB, and the E2 note 4.8 c sharp), and Eb4 and F5 carry neither

the string's measured torsion on D3 (`torsion-measured mansour-2016-kaplan-cello-d3-open`; Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2016, Part 2, section 2.2): 10 twist modes at multiples of 758 Hz, a characteristic impedance of 1.8 kg/s and Q 34 on every mode, a non-dispersive line from the nut to the bridge station with the after-length untwisted and no gas drag added. The binding of that string to this one is a reading of the two papers (Part 2 names neither the string's make nor its length; the row binds it to Part 1's Kaplan Solutions D3 at 0.69 m). On the body with the endpin and the printed bar, before the other strings were added, it moves D3 1.0 c flat (146.91 Hz) and off the render clock (326.73 samples a period, steady to 1.4 c), moves H2 to H10 by 2.9 dB or less re the first and leaves 14 of 14 rows inside
a bow of finite width (a 10 mm ribbon) with hair compliance, driven by a gesture schedule of ramp, hold and lift; on D3 and A3 the bow force follows the bow speed through the start of the stroke

on E3, E2, F5 and Eb4 the bow sits 1/11 of the sounding length from the bridge, as on the open pages (25.1 mm of 276.6 mm, 50.1 mm of 551.0 mm, 20.0 mm of 220.5 mm and 44.4 mm of 487.9 mm), with the force from Schelleng's limits at that distance (the maximum goes as v/beta and the minimum as v/beta^2: Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2017, eqs 3-5). The force is the geometric mean of the window, a rule chosen for these pages and stated before any render (E3 1.47 N in 0.47 to 4.60 N, E2 1.50 N in 0.49 to 4.60 N, F5 0.33 N in 0.062 to 1.78 N on the A string, Eb4 0.29 N in 0.048 to 1.78 N on the A string, where Eb4's window uses the shell table with each mode's Q rebuilt for the page's wood loss). The open pages' forces sit higher in their windows by the same arithmetic (A3's 0.7071 N and D3's 1.0 N at 0.80 and 0.78 on a log scale from the minimum to the maximum), F5's old 0.7071 N was 1.10 times Schelleng's maximum at its old distance, and Eb4's old 0.7071 N was inside its window then, at 0.85 on that scale
the measured rosin friction curve (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13) on every note
the printed 116 mm after-length, bridge to tailpiece (Fouilhe and Houssay, SMAC 2013), on every note

stopped notes: a rigid finger stop on the fingerboard (Issanchou 2017) at 1e12 N/m on the C string (E2, E3) and 1e13 N/m on the A string (F5, and Eb4 as its page), placed at the equal-tempered station and then moved once toward the named note, never toward the recording, on E2, E3 and F5; Eb4's finger is not moved
Eb4 rendered at 47944 Hz, a rate chosen so its period is a whole number of samples, and resampled to 48 kHz for the page

Eb4 plays with the body's wood loss raised 3.25 times; on free decay that takes the shell's lower strong pole from Q 67-75 with wood alone to Q 24-27, read on F5 and C2 renders with the same packs, near the 18-26 printed for a cello on a rig (Zhang and Woodhouse 2014); every other cello page keeps the wood-only loss

on A3, D3, C2, G2, E2, E3 and Eb4, the endpin as a point mass of 186.6 g on the shell: 0.47 m by 8 mm (Sakai and Samejima 2023, Table 3) at the 7900 kg/m3 printed there for iron, solid assumed, shared over the lower end block's 85 by 30 mm footprint from Johannsson's table, a maker's table not measured on this cello; the block's own wood is not added

on A3, D3, C2, G2, E2, E3 and Eb4, the bass bar at its printed place: its ends sit 83.5 and 83.4 mm from the top's ends, against 80 to 85 mm on Alan Goldblatt's cello specification sheet and 80 in a maker's forum post (Cliff Green), after sliding it 12.27 mm toward the neck from where the il Cannone mapping had put it (71.2 and 95.7 mm); its length, height, width, slant and place under the bridge's bass foot are unchanged. Goldblatt's and Johannsson's are makers' tables, borrowed and named, not measurements of this cello

on G2 and D3, the cello's other three strings on the same bridge, unbowed and undamped, so they ring only as the body drives them: on G2 the D3, C2 and A3 strings of Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2016 (D'Addario Kaplan Solutions KS510), each as its own open page plays it but single plane and with 36, 64 and 24 retained bending modes (to 4.1-4.6 kHz; the residual-flexibility row condenses what is left out); on D3 the C2 (64 modes), G2 (56) and A3 (24) strings, single plane (to 4.1-5.0 kHz), C2 and A3 of the same set and G2 the Thomastik-Infeld Dominant that its own open page plays (Lampis, Mayer and Chatziioannou 2024); the bridge joint is the card's 200000 N/m, 0.1 N s/m on each, and the body profile carries four bridge lines (G, D, C, A on G2; D, C, G, A on D3) on the same table and endpin block
physics_missing: a measured cello: the body is computed from published geometry and wood data, and no measured body admittance or string Q of this instrument is on the cards; on the C2 page the wood data are stated only from 150 Hz (maple) and 100 Hz (spruce), so that body has no mode below 150 Hz, above the C2 fundamental

body modes above the computed range: 256 modes end at 2438.5 Hz (2209.9 Hz in the modal run on the 24-layer ribs of C2, E2, E3 and Eb4; the 512 modes of D3 and A3 at about 4.3 kHz, read for D3); the plates are resolved to about 3 kHz and the 6-layer ribs not above about 1 kHz

body damping: the shell's lowest strong pole reads Q 72-78 from wood alone (free decay 67-75, receiver sweep 78), against 18 to 26 printed for a cello on a rig or foam and 13.4 held by a player (Zhang and Woodhouse 2014); the F5 page names this as a likely reason for its fault, not shown. The wood loss raised 3.25 times toward the printed damping was tried on all eight cello pages: one rose (Eb4, 10 to 11 of 14) and it darkened every page, bringing the three too-bright pages toward their recordings and the five too-dark ones away. So more wood loss isn't what the cello's top end is missing
a body-radiation skin row: the posted cards carry none

a bow that varies during the note: force and speed hold after the ramp (D3's and A3's force follows speed only through the start), so the notes repeat too exactly: harmonics-to-noise reads 37.7 dB against 30.1 in the recording on C2 and 43.2 against 30.1 on E2 (Eb4, with the printed wood loss, its bow at 1/11 and 24-layer ribs, reads 39.2 against 37.9, where its 6-layer page read 41.8); the Eb4 attack builds in 437 ms against 411, where its 6-layer page's built in 342

time-step independence: at 48 kHz a note's period can lock to the render clock and put lines into the sound that are not in the instrument; Eb4 needed its own render rate, and F5 held a line at exactly a third of its pitch (233.0 Hz, -28.8 dB) until its bow moved to 1/11 of its sounding length, which removed it

an explanation of the finger: the bowed pitch moves 1.4 to 1.8 times the length of the move (E3 25.3 c for 17.6 c before its residual row, which takes a further 4.5 c off the note, E2 19.2 c for 10.7 c before its row, which takes a further 4.8 c up), so E2 and E3 land flat of equal temperament, and the E3 and F5 recordings sit sharp of it

the bow's omitted-mode compliance on a stopped note: the engine refuses `bow-residual-flexibility` with a finger stop (the bow/stop cross-compliance is not yet carried), so E2 and E3 have the support row only and Eb4 and F5 have neither row; F5 was tried with the support row and fell from 9 to 8 of 15 (harmonics-to-noise left its ruler, the third harmonic rose to 23.7 dB re the first, and a held line appeared at 189 Hz, -19 dB), so it stays without

the timbre balance: the low notes and A3 are too dark (centroid 217 Hz against 388 on C2, 196 against 390 on E2, 220 against 575 on E3, 353 against 868 on A3) and F5 too bright (1587 against 1187; Eb4, with the printed wood loss, its bow at 1/11 and 24-layer ribs, is 499 against 466, where its 6-layer page was 466); D3's first two harmonics are swapped without the other strings on its bridge (H2 4.6 dB over H1, the recording 7.5 dB under) and in the recording's order with them (10.3 dB under), where its centroid is 311 Hz against 215 and its third harmonic sits 12.2 dB over the recording's; on F5 the second and third harmonics now sit 3.8 and 3.6 dB over the first (the third 15.7 dB over it before), the recording 4.6 and 5.9 dB under it

the stopped notes' bow: E3 at 1/11 and the page's 0.4204 N broke to its octave (0.90 times Schelleng's minimum, rendered 11-04). With the bow at 1/11 the E3 holes at H4 and H5 did not close (they moved -0.8 and +2.7 dB re the first on the 6-layer page rendered 11-05), and they sit in a valley of that 6-layer shell's bridge mobility at 818-870 Hz; on the posted E3 clip, with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs, H4 and H5 sit 16.5 and 30.3 dB under the recording's re the first (0.7-1.4 s); E2, with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs, holds its level within 0.5 dB from 0.2 to 2.4 s, its second harmonic leads its first by 8.4 dB (+5.5 in the recording, 0.5-1.4 s), and its burst near the body's 190 Hz mode, which no grader row measures, reads -59.7 dB re the strongest bin over 1.0-1.7 s (the recording shows nothing there above -51.7 dB); F5 at 1/11 with 0.33 N is clean in its motion (no octave, no subharmonic) but now reads 34.6 dB harmonics-to-noise against 27.6 in the recording, and its harmonics-to-noise, cepstral and harmonics rows left their rulers while wavelet, odd/even and attack came in (9 of 15 both ways); Eb4 at 1/11 with 0.29 N, on the 6-layer page rendered 11-06, is clean in its motion (no octave, no subharmonic, one full slip per period as before, with more small slips between them: 8.2, 2.8 and 12.0 slip events per period on its three bow cells against 2.1, 2.0 and 4.0) and ties its page at 11 of 14 (attack comes inside, cepstral envelope goes outside), but it now reads 41.8 dB harmonics-to-noise against 37.9 in the recording and holds a line at 301.3 Hz, -39.1 dB re its first harmonic, where the last page read -57.5 dB. The stopped notes' force is a rule chosen for these pages, the window's geometric mean; the open pages' forces sit higher (0.78 to 0.80 on a log scale); a measured player's bow force for a stopped cello note at a known bow distance would replace the rule

lines that are not harmonics: C2's line near 175 Hz reads 176.8 Hz, 23.4 dB over the recording over 0.5-1.4 s, and its line near 163.9 Hz reads 165.4 Hz, 8.8 dB over the recording's there; neither is traced; Eb4's strongest line that is not a harmonic is 301.3 Hz, 12.2 Hz under its note: with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs it reads -46.4 dB re its first harmonic over 0.72-2.17 s (-39.1 dB on the 6-layer page), where the recording's strongest line between 285 and 304 Hz is 304.0 Hz at -48.5 dB; the 6-layer page matched it in frequency to a shell mode near 300 Hz, but in the modal run that mode moves from 300.5 to 294.9 Hz from 6 to 24 layers (the bar moved on both) and the line does not, so it is not traced; summed over 165-195 Hz its cluster reads -30.6 dB re its first harmonic, against -32.3 dB on the 6-layer page and -32.7 dB in the recording; no grader row measures either

the other strings: only G2 (D3, C2 and A3 on its bridge) and D3 (C2, G2 and A3 on its bridge) carry them, unbowed and undamped; every other page has only its bowed string, so there is no sympathetic ringing or string-to-string coupling through the body there, and the strings added have no torsion, no fingers and no dampers. C2 was tried, on its 6-layer ribs, with the same kind of three strings (D3, G2 and A3 at 36, 52 and 24 modes) and fell from 6 to 5 of 14 (its centroid crosses out and its 179 Hz body line rises 8.3 dB), so C2 stays without them. On G2 they cost: harmonics-to-noise 38.6 to 31.0 dB (recording 36.3), partial frequencies 0.30 to 3.81 c, attack 73 to 57 ms (recording 175), a stable line at 146.2 Hz at -30.6 dB re the strongest bin (the D3 string ringing), and the eighth harmonic 19.7 dB lower, 23.5 dB under the recording's. On D3 they cost: harmonics-to-noise 39.2 to 31.7 dB (recording 43.3), the odd/even balance -5.8 to -0.9 dB (recording -6.3), the onset shelf (the attack reads 91 ms where it read 387, against 381 in the recording, which the shelf had matched without a slow rise; the row is now 2.06 against a ruler of 2.28, the nearest of the fourteen to its edge), spectral flux 1.04 to 1.15, the note 1.2 c sharper than the last page's (147.01 Hz), and a stable line at 198.3 Hz at -33.1 dB re the first harmonic that rings down and is not traced to a string: 11 dB over the recording's strongest low line and 7 dB over the last page's
the rosin's temperature-dependent behaviour, transfer layer and contact history: eq. 13 is a velocity law measured at steady sliding
the endpin's floor contact and the player's hold on the ribs: the point mass on A3, D3, C2, G2, E2, E3 and Eb4 carries neither, and neither is modelled

torsion on the other strings and on stopped notes: only the open D3 string has a measured torsion row (Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2016, Part 2); the row refuses a stop profile, so the stopped notes cannot take it, and no other string of the set is measured. D3's own torsion row did not close any of its holes: with the endpin and the printed bar and no other strings, re the strongest harmonic over 1.0-1.9 s, H5, H7 and H9 sit 9.1, 8.5 and 12.3 dB under the recording and H3, H8 and H10 14.2, 11.3 and 35.4 dB over it, and its centroid is 358 Hz against 215
